title: Ban on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy levels
requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (one using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Vendors may not sell, license or provide such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
key_value: Ban; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)
coverage_conditions: All landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley, and vendors providing coordinated pricing algorithms to them.
exemptions: Aggregated anonymous rental data products that do not recommend rents or terms; tools for government affordable-housing rent or income limits; market research for financing or appraisals, and software research, testing or training, if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only if the landlord uses a coordinated pricing algorithm relying on nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old.

citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S.
quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
conflict_note: Effective date unresolved. Ord. 7,992-N.S., which amends the pre-existing Chapter 13.63, was passed to print on 2025-11-18 and appears on a 2025-12-02 second-reading agenda. No effective date is stated for either the amendment or the original chapter. Status in_force assumes final adoption. State AB 325 (Bus. & Prof. Code 16729) also applies, but the corpus shows no preemption.

title: Required Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement
requirement: An owner who charges an application or credit-report fee must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement before receiving the fee. The owner must also state the maximum fee permitted under Civ. Code 1950.6(b).
coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of Berkeley residential property who charge screening or application fees.
quoted_span: The “Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement” shall mean the following statement or a substantially similar statement:
conflict_note: The URL required in the statement is still to be provided by the City, and the effective date is not stated.

title: Ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Contrary lease terms are unenforceable.
coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, including existing leases.
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance (2026 amounts, annually inflation-adjusted)
requirement: Owners evicting a tenant for owner move-in must pay relocation assistance. The Rent Board must adjust the amounts each year for inflation (Measure BB).
coverage_conditions: Tenants in units covered by the Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance who are evicted for owner move-in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to owner move-in evictions; the additional payment depends on household qualifying criteria.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (relocation provisions), as amended by Measure BB
quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.
conflict_note: The effective date is for the 2026 amount adjustment approved 2025-10-16, not the original ordinance.

title: Ellis Act withdrawal relocation assistance (2026 amounts)
requirement: Owners who evict tenants to withdraw a property from the rental market must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions.
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley evicted for an Ellis Act withdrawal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to Ellis Act withdrawals; the additional payment depends on household qualifying criteria.

quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.
conflict_note: The effective date is for the 2026 amount adjustment, not the original ordinance.

title: Berkeley just cause for eviction (fully and partially covered units)
requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may not be evicted without just cause.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units: pre-1980 multifamily units, single-family homes, rooming houses, post-1980 new construction, most condominiums, and subsidized units.
exemptions: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied); shared kitchen or bath with an owner resident at tenancy start; post-2018-11-07 tenancies on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy for the Golden Duplex, shared-facility and ADU exemptions; dormitory or cooperative status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
conflict_note: No code section or enactment date is given. State Civ. Code 1946.2 yields to this local ordinance.

title: No nonpayment eviction for debt below one month's Fair Market Rent
requirement: Eviction for nonpayment is allowed only if rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont) for an equivalent-size unit.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is no longer permitted for rental debt of less than one month’s Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated.

title: No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease
requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated.

title: Stricter requirements for lease-breach evictions
requirement: Lease-breach evictions require breach of a material agreed term, actual harm to the landlord, and proof that the tenant's conduct was unreasonable. The notice must clearly describe the breach.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated.

title: Eviction notice content and Rent Board filing within 3 business days
requirement: Termination notices must refer tenants to Rent Board counseling. Copies of termination notices, notices to quit, and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days of service.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated.

title: Berkeley rent ceilings: Annual General Adjustment (2026: 1.0%; Measure BB cap 5%)
requirement: For fully covered units, landlords may raise rent ceilings only by the Annual General Adjustment (65% of Bay Area CPI change), capped at 5% under Measure BB. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, effective no earlier than 2026-01-01, and requires Reg. 1148 eligibility and notice. Banked AGAs may still be used to reach the ceiling.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 (new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980 is not rent-controlled); single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses with 5 or more individually rented rooms; certain subsidized units.
exemptions: No rent ceiling for: post-June-1980 new construction; single-family homes with tenancies starting on or after 1996-01-01; most condominiums; certain HUD-financed subsidized units. Fully exempt: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied on 1979-12-31 and now); units sharing a kitchen or bath with an owner who lived there when the tenancy began; post-2018-11-07 tenancies on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives. The 2026 AGA excludes tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01 with Costa-Hawkins-set rents.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy start dates (single-family homes before 1996; Costa-Hawkins tenancies from 2025); condominium status; owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, ADU); subsidy type and HUD mortgage; rooming-house configuration; Reg. 1148 eligibility and notice.

citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.76.110A; Rent Board Reg. 1148; Rent Ordinance as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.
conflict_note: Sources describe the cutoff both as 'built before 1980' and as 'certificate of occupancy after June 1980'. This record uses a CofO on or before 1980-06-30. The effective date shown is for the 2026 AGA; Measure BB's effective date is not stated. State AB 1482 yields where this stricter local rent control applies.

title: Government-owned or subsidized units covered by the Rent Ordinance (Measure BB)
requirement: Government-owned or subsidized units (e.g., Section 8 vouchers, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME) are fully or partially covered, must register, and pay a registration fee. Fully covered subsidized units have an AGA-limited rent ceiling.
coverage_conditions: Government-owned or subsidized units in Berkeley.
exemptions: Section 202 and 811 units, and Rent Supplement, Section 8 LMSA and project-based Section 8 units in projects with HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgages, are only partially covered (no rent ceiling).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Subsidy type and HUD mortgage status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Government-owned or -subsidized rental units become either fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated.

title: Rent increase petitions only for completed capital improvements
requirement: Landlords may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements. Preliminary authorization for planned improvements is no longer available.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units subject to the rent ceiling.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).
conflict_note: Effective date not stated.

title: Utility charges must be built into base rent unless separately metered
requirement: For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06 in fully covered units, utilities may be charged only as a set amount in base rent, or where separately metered and in the tenant's name. Adding utility costs to the ceiling requires a Rent Board petition.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units; tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06.
exemptions: Separately metered utilities in the tenant's name as specified in the lease.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy start date on or after 2024-02-06; metering arrangement.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Utility charges must be a set amount incorporated into the base rent at the start of a tenancy unless the utility is separately metered and the account is in the tenant’s name as specified in the lease.
conflict_note: The 2024-02-06 applicability date predates the November 2024 Measure BB election. It may be a retroactive application or an error.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, terminating a tenancy, or charging higher rent or deposit based on criminal history.
key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use banned; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
coverage_conditions: Current and prospective tenants of rental housing in Berkeley.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing and Section 8 properties; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties where an owner of record lives on site as a primary residence; owner move-back agreements under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding or replacing roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy as primary residence for the 1-3 unit exemption; public housing/Section 8 status; owner move-back agreements; sublet or roommate situations.

quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
conflict_note: Passed 2020-04-14; effective date not stated in the corpus.

title: Annual interest on security deposits
requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units must pay interest on security deposits each year, plus a prorated amount at move-out.
coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
exemptions: Golden Duplex; shared kitchen or bath with a resident owner; owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after 2018-11-07); dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy exemptions; dormitory or cooperative status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
conflict_note: The interest rate and section number are not given in the corpus.

title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744): not enacted
requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement tenant eviction protections. It was sent to a study order on 2024-09-09 and was not enacted.
coverage_conditions: Boston residential tenants (proposed).
quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.

title: Housing Stability Notification Act: Notice of Tenants' Rights with notice to quit or non-renewal
requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must give the Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with any notice to quit or non-renewal, and must file a copy with the City.
key_value: Warning for 1st offense; $300/day for later offenses
coverage_conditions: All Boston landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or occupancy.
exemptions: Hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities; nonprofit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when a tenancy is being ended or not renewed.

citation: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (Oct. 2020); penalties Sec. 10-11.7
quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
conflict_note: This is a notice requirement, not a just-cause standard, and a violation does not halt an eviction. Sec. 10-11.7 may be only the penalty section.

title: Boston rent stabilization home rule petition (H.3744, 193rd session): not enacted
requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement rent stabilization. It was sent to a study order (H5035) on 2024-09-09 and died when the session ended. It is not law.
coverage_conditions: Boston residential rentals (proposed).
quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
conflict_note: M.G.L. c. 40P § 4 bars local rent control without state authorization, which is why a home rule petition was needed.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy: criminal history limits (funded and inclusionary units)
requirement: Covered providers must assess applicants individually rather than use blanket bans. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old.
key_value: Convictions older than 5 years may not be considered
coverage_conditions: Housing receiving DND funding or land, or BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units.
exemptions: Direct relationship to the housing or an unreasonable safety risk; current criminal behavior; conflicting federal or state requirements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted housing.

citation: Boston DND, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction.
conflict_note: An administrative policy, not an ordinance. Its current status in 2026 is not confirmed, and the source is a shared-drive copy.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy: credit score and history limits
requirement: Covered providers may not use credit scores to approve or deny applicants. Credit history may be used only in place of unavailable rental history, and lack of credit is not grounds for rejection.
coverage_conditions: DND-funded or BPDA IDP income-restricted housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted housing.

citation: Boston DND, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing
conflict_note: An administrative policy whose current status is not confirmed.

title: Boston fair housing ban, including rental assistance discrimination
requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting based on protected classes, including rental assistance (e.g., Section 8), family status and military status.
coverage_conditions: Any housing rented in Boston.
citation: City of Boston fair housing law (Boston Fair Housing Commission; code section not stated)
quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.
conflict_note: No ordinance citation, effective date or exemptions are given.

title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in a conspiracy to restrain trade (AB 325)
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade under the Cartwright Act. A common pricing algorithm is one used by two or more persons that relies on competitor data. This applies to rental pricing.
coverage_conditions: Any person other than the end consumer; not limited to housing.
exemptions: End consumers.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy in restraint of trade.

citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
conflict_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06. The 2026-01-01 effective date is inferred from California's default rule.

title: Ban on coercing adoption of common pricing algorithm recommendations (AB 325)
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm while coercing another person to adopt the price or commercial term it recommends.
coverage_conditions: Any person other than the end consumer in California.
exemptions: End consumers.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion to adopt the algorithm's recommendation.

quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
conflict_note: The 2026-01-01 effective date is inferred from California's default rule.

title: Application screening fee capped at actual cost and $30 (CPI-adjusted)
requirement: Screening fees may not exceed actual out-of-pocket costs plus the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998-01-01.
coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents screening residential applicants, including guarantors and cosigners.
exemptions: Fee rules of federal or state housing assistance programs are not preempted.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Housing assistance program fee rules may govern instead.

citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) (as amended by Stats. 2025, ch. 67, AB 1170)
quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
conflict_note: 2026-01-01 is the effective date of the current amended text; the $30 CPI-indexed cap predates it. The 2026 figure of $68.96 is reported by the Berkeley Rent Board.

title: No screening fee when no unit is available
requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when it knows or should know that no unit is available now or within a reasonable period.
coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents charging screening fees.
quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
conflict_note: 2026-01-01 is the effective date of the current text; an earlier version of the provision existed.

title: Screening fee only with a first-come process or a refund to non-selected applicants
requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if it offers one of two options. The first is a first-come process with written criteria that charges only applicants actually considered. The second is a refund to applicants not selected, within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission.
key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission
coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents charging screening fees.
exemptions: No refund under the first-come option for applicants denied for failing the criteria.
quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

title: Itemized receipt for screening fee; return of unused portion
requirement: The landlord must give a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, and must return any portion of the fee not used for authorized purposes.
coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents collecting screening fees.
quoted_span: (d) The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

title: Copy of credit report to fee-paying applicant within 7 days
requirement: If the applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord must provide a copy of the consumer credit report within 7 days of receiving it.
coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents collecting screening fees.
quoted_span: (f) If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.

title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction (AB 1482)
requirement: After 12 months of lawful occupancy (24 months if adult tenants were added), owners may terminate only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. No-fault terminations require relocation of one month's rent, paid within 15 days or as a waiver of the final month's rent.
key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including mobilehome park units, not covered by a qualifying local just cause ordinance.
exemptions: Transient hotels; care facilities; dormitories; units sharing a kitchen or bath with a resident owner; owner-occupied single-family homes renting up to 2 units or bedrooms (including ADU/JADU); owner-occupied duplexes; housing with a CofO issued within the previous 15 years; separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, if notice is given; deed-restricted affordable housing; properties under a qualifying local just cause ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy length (12/24 months); for separately alienable single-family homes or condos, owner entity type and whether the exemption notice was given; owner occupancy; affordable-housing restrictions; whether a local just cause ordinance applies.

interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
conflict_note: The current version has been operative since 2024-04-01 and was last amended by AB 1529, effective 2026-01-01. Original AB 1482 protections date to 2020. Repealed 2030-01-01. Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted by 2019-09-01 or more protective later ones. owner_exemption_max_units is 3 (owner-occupied single-family home plus ADU/JADU); condo units in larger buildings may also be exempt if natural-person-owned.

title: Temporary relocation for capital improvement displacement under 20 days (San Francisco)
requirement: In San Francisco, relocation for temporary capital-improvement displacements of less than 20 days is governed by Civ. Code 1947.9 rather than Rent Ordinance 37.9C.
coverage_conditions: Temporary capital-improvement displacements in San Francisco lasting less than 20 days.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Displacement must be temporary, for capital improvements, and less than 20 days.

quoted_span: *The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
conflict_note: The daily amount comes from the SF Rent Board rates page (c142). Displaces SF § 37.9C for displacements under 20 days.

title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act, AB 1482)
requirement: Over any 12 months, gross rent may not rise more than 5% plus regional CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months. Increases are limited to 2 per 12 months.
coverage_conditions: California residential real property, excluding housing with a CofO issued within the previous 15 years and other listed exemptions.
exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; CofO within the previous 15 years; separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, if notice is given; owner-occupied duplexes (no ADU/JADU); mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner entity type and exemption notice for separately alienable units; owner occupancy of a duplex; affordable-housing restrictions; dormitory status; whether stricter local rent control applies.

interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
conflict_note: Effective dates differ by source. The LAHD page implies 2020-01-01 (AB 1482). The statute text says the current version (SB 567) has been operative since 2024-04-01, and that the cap reaches increases on or after 2019-03-15. Repealed 2030-01-01. Yields to stricter local rent control. The LAHD page's 8.9% figure is outdated.

title: FEHA limits on criminal history in tenant screening
requirement: Providers may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not impose blanket bans. Conviction-based denials must be directly related to tenancy suitability.
key_value: No arrest-only, sealed/expunged or juvenile records; no blanket bans
coverage_conditions: Most California housing providers and screening companies.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person; certain shared-living, senior and homeless-youth housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy when renting to one additional person.

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
conflict_note: Agency summary page; no section number cited.

title: FEHA housing discrimination ban, including source of income and discriminatory screening
requirement: Owners and screening companies may not discriminate or screen on protected characteristics, including source of income (e.g., Section 8 vouchers). They may not advertise 'No Section 8' or refuse to complete subsidy paperwork.
coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations in California, advertisers, and tenant screening companies.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (discriminatory advertising remains prohibited); qualifying senior housing; shared-living single-sex preferences. Asking about the level or source of income is not discrimination.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy when renting to one additional person; senior housing qualification.

quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
conflict_note: The most recent amendment is SB 267, effective 2024-01-01; the original effective date is not given.

title: Credit history for subsidized applicants requires an alternative-evidence option
requirement: Where a government rent subsidy is involved, a provider may not use credit history unless it lets the applicant provide verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent.
coverage_conditions: Applicants with a government rent subsidy.
exemptions: Owners may still verify employment, references and identity.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a government rent subsidy is involved.

quoted_span: (B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay

title: Income standard for subsidized tenants based only on the tenant's portion of rent
requirement: Where a government rent subsidy is involved, income or financial standards must be based only on the portion of rent the tenant pays.
coverage_conditions: Applicants with a government rent subsidy.
exemptions: Owners may still verify employment, references and identity.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a government rent subsidy is involved.

quoted_span: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

title: Income standards must count co-residents' aggregate income
requirement: Income standards must count the combined income of persons residing together on the same basis as married persons' combined income.
